verses.text: And Solomon, the son of David, strengthened himself over his kingdom, and Yahweh his God {was} with him and made him great to above.
And Solomon spoke to all of Israel, to the commanders of thousands and hundreds and to the judges and to every leader in all of Israel, the heads of fathers.
And Solomon went, and all of the assembly with him, to the high place that {was} at Gibeon, for the tent of meeting of God was there, which Moses, the servant of Yahweh, had made in the wilderness.
But David had brought up the Box of God from Kiriath Jearim to {where} David had prepared for it, for he had stretched out a tent for it in Jerusalem.
And the altar of bronze that Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had made {was} there to the face of the tabernacle of Yahweh, and Solomon and the assembly sought him.
And Solomon went up there to the altar of bronze, to the face of Yahweh, which {was} at the tent of meeting, and he brought up onto it 1,000 burnt offerings.
In that night, God appeared to Solomon, and he said to him, “Ask! What I shall give to you?”
And Solomon said to God, “You, you did great covenant faithfulness with David my father, and you have made me reign in his place.
Now, Yahweh God, may your word with David my father be confirmed, for you, you have made me reign over a people numerous as the dust of the earth.
Now give wisdom and knowledge to me, that I may go out to the face of this people and that I may come in, for who shall judge this your great people?”

And God said to Solomon, “Because this was with your heart, and you have not requested wealth, riches, or honor or the life of the ones hating you, and you have also not requested many days, but you have requested wisdom and knowledge for yourself that you might judge my people, over whom I have made you reign,
wisdom and knowledge are given to you, and I will give to you wealth and riches and honor that were not thus to the kings who were to your face and will not be thus after you.”
And Solomon came from the high place that {was} at Gibeon {to} Jerusalem, from the face of the tent of meeting, and he reigned over Israel.
And Solomon accumulated chariotry and horsemen. And 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen were to him. And he stationed them in the cities of chariotry and with the king in Jerusalem.
And the king made silver and gold in Jerusalem like stones, and he made cedars like the sycamores that {are} in the Shephelah for abundance.
And the going out of the horses that {were} to Solomon {was} from Egypt and from Kue. The traders of the king took from Kue at a price.
And they brought up and brought out from Egypt a chariot for 600 silver and a horse for 150. And thus by their hand they brought out to all of the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
And Solomon said to build a house for the name of Yahweh and a house for his kingdom.
And Solomon numbered 70,000, a man, a bearer, and 80,000, a man, a quarrier in the hill country, and ones overseeing over them, 3,600.
And Solomon sent to Hiram, the king of Tyre, saying, “As that you did with David my father and sent to him cedars to build for himself a house to dwell in it,

behold, I am building a house for the name of Yahweh my God, to consecrate to him, to burn to his face incense of spices, and for the perpetual arrangement and burnt offerings in the morning and in the evening, on the Sabbaths and on the new moons and at the annual festivals of Yahweh our God. Forever this {is} upon Israel.
Now the house that I am building {shall be} great, for our God {is} greater than all gods.

But who can retain strength to build a house for him, since the heavens and the heavens of the heavens do not contain him? And who {am} I, that I should build a house for him, except to sacrifice to his face?

And now, send to me a wise man to work in gold and in silver and in bronze and in iron and in purple and crimson and violet, one also knowing {how} to engrave engravings, with the wise who {are} with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father prepared.
And send to me trees of cedar, cypress, and algum from Lebanon, for I, I know that your servants are knowing {how} to cut trees of Lebanon. And behold, my servants {will be} with your servants,
even to prepare for me trees in abundance, for the house that I am building {will be} great, and it will be wonderful.
And behold, to the hewers, to the cutters of the trees, I will give crushed wheat to your servants, 20,000 cors, and barley, 20,000 cors, and wine 20,000 baths, and oil, 20, 000 baths.”
And Hiram, the king of Tyre, said in a writing that he sent to Solomon, “Because Yahweh loves his people, he has made you king over them.”

And Hiram said, “Blessed {be} Yahweh, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth, who has given to King David a son of wisdom, knowing insight and understanding, who will build a house for Yahweh and a house for his kingdom.
And now, I have sent a wise man, knowing understanding, Huram Abi,

the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, and his father a man of Tyre, knowing {how} to work in gold and in silver, in bronze, in iron, in stones and in wood, in purple, in violet, and in linen and in crimson, and {how} to engrave any engraving and to devise any device that is given to him, with your wise {ones} and the wise {ones} of my lord David, your father.
And now, the wheat and the barley, the oil and the wine that my lord has said, let him send to his servants.
And we, we will cut trees from Lebanon, according to all of your need, and we will bring them to you {as} rafts upon the sea {to} Joppa, and you, you will bring them up {to} Jerusalem.”
And Solomon numbered all of the men, the foreigners who {were} in the land of Israel, after the counting that David his father had counted them. And they were found {to be} 153,600.
And from them he made 70,000, a bearer, and 80,000. a quarrier in the hill country, and 3,600 ones overseeing to make the people work.

And Solomon began to build the house of Yahweh in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where he had appeared to David his father, where David had prepared, in the place at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
And he began to build in the second month, on the second, in the year of four to his reign.
And these {were} the founding of Solomon to build the house of God. The length {in} cubits, by the former measure, {was} 60 cubits, and the width {was} 20 cubits.
And the porch that {was} on the face of the length on the face of the width of the house {was} 20 cubits, and its height {was} 120. And he overlaid it from within {with} pure gold.
And he covered the great house with wood of cypress, and he covered it with pure gold, and he brought up palm trees and chains onto it.
And he overlaid the house {with} precious stone for beauty, and the gold {was} gold of Parvaim.
And he covered the house, the beams, the thresholds, and its walls and its doors {with} gold, and he engraved cherubs on the walls.
And he made the house of the Holy of Holies. Its length on the face of the width of the house {was} 20 cubits, and its width {was} 20 cubits. And he covered it {with} pure gold, to 600 kikkars.
And the weight of the nails {was} to 50 shekels {of} gold. And he covered the upper chambers {with} gold.
And he made in the house of the Holy of Holies two cherubs, a work of carving, and he overlaid them {with} gold.

And the wings of the cherubs, their length {was} 20 cubits. A wing of the one was to 5 cubits, reaching to the wall of the house, and the other wing {was} 5 cubits, reaching to a wing of the other cherub.
And a wing of the other cherub {was} 5 cubits, reaching to the wall of the house, and the other wing {was} 5 cubits, joining to the wing of the other cherub.
The wings of these cherubs were spreading out 20 cubits. And they were standing on their feet, and their faces {were} toward the house.
And he made a curtain {of} violet and purple and crimson and linen, and he brought cherubs up onto it.
And he made two pillars to the face of the house, 35 cubits {was} the length, and the capital that was on its head {was} five cubits.
And he made chains {as} in the inner sanctuary, and he put {them} on the head of the pillars, and he made 100 pomegranates, and he put {them} on the chains.
And he set up the pillars on the face of the temple, one from the right and one from the left. And he called the name of the right Jakin and the name of the left Boaz.
And he made an altar of bronze. Its length (was) 20 cubits, and its width (was) 20 cubits, and its height {was} 10 cubits.
And he made a cast sea, ten by the cubit from its lip to its lip, circular around. And five by the cubit {was} its height, and a cord of thirty by the cubit surrounded it around.
And a likeness of oxen {was} below to it around, around, surrounding it, ten in a cubit, encircling the sea around. Oxen {in} two rows were cast in its casting.

It was standing on twelve oxen, three facing north and three facing west and three facing south and three facing east, and the sea {was} upon them from above. And all of their hindquarters {were} inward.
And its thickness {was} a handbreadth, and its lip {was} like the work of the lip of a cup, the blossom of a lily. Taking hold, it contained 3,000 baths.

And he made ten basins, and he put five on the right and five on the left, to wash in them. They would rinse the work of the burnt offering in them. And the Sea {was} for washing for the priests in it.
And he made ten lampstands of gold according to their ordinance, and he put five on the right and five on the left in the temple.
And he made ten tables and rested {them} in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. And he made 100 bowls of gold.
And he made the courtyard of the priests and the great court and the doors for the court, and he overlaid their doors {with} bronze.
And he put the Sea from the shoulder of the right, eastward toward the south.
And Huram made basins and shovels and bowls.
the two pillars, and the bowls, the capitals on the head of the two pillars, and the two networks for covering the two bowls of the capitals that {were} on the head of the pillars,
and the 400 pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for one network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that {were} on the faces of the pillars.
And he made stands, and he made basins on the stands,
one sea and 12 oxen beneath it,
and the pots and the shovels and the forks. And all of the vessels Huram Abi made for King Solomon for the house of Yahweh {were} polished bronze.
In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the thickness of the ground between Succoth and between Zaredathah.
And Solomon made all of these vessels in great abundance, so the weight of the bronze was not sought out.
And Solomon made all of the vessels that {were} {for} the house of God: the altar of gold and the tables that on them {was} the bread of the face
and the lampstands and their lamps for their burning according to the ordinance to the face of the inner sanctuary, purified gold,
and the blossom and the lamps and the tongs, gold, it {was} perfections of gold,

and the trimmers and the sprinkling bowls and the palms and the firepans, purified gold, and the entrance of the house, its inner doors to the Holy of Holies, and the doors of the house, for the temple, gold,

And all of the work that Solomon did for the house of Yahweh was complete. And Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father. And he put the silver and the gold and all of the vessels in the storerooms of the house of God.

Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all of the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers of the sons of Israel, to Jerusalem to bring up the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh from the City of David, that {is}, Zion.
And every man of Israel, they assembled to the king at the feast; it {was} the seventh month.
And all of the elders of Israel came, and the Levites carried the Box.
And they brought up the Box and the tent of meeting and all of the sacred vessels that {were} in the tent. The priests {and} the Levites brought them up.

And King Solomon and all of the congregation of Israel having gathered themselves to him {were} to the face of the Box, sacrificing sheep and cattle that were not counted and were not numbered from abundance.
And the priests brought in the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh to its place, to the inner sanctuary of the house, to the Holy of Holies, to under the wings of the cherubs.
And the cherubs were spreading out wings over the place of the Box. And the cherubs covered over the Box and over its poles from above.
And the poles were long, and the heads of the poles from the Box were seen at the face of the inner sanctuary, but they were not seen {from} the outside. And they are there to this day.
Nothing {was} in the Box except the two tablets that Moses had placed at Horeb, where Yahweh cut with the sons of Israel when they came out from Egypt.
And it happened, when the priests came out from the holy place (for all of the priests who were found had consecrated themselves, without keeping to the divisions),

and the Levites, the singers, as for all of them, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and their brothers, clothed {in} linen, with cymbals and with lyres and harps, were standing east of the altar, and with them {were} 120 priests blowing trumpets,

that it happened, the trumpeters and singers {were} like one to sound one voice to praise and thank Yahweh, and as they raised a voice with trumpets and with cymbals and with instruments of song, and when they praised Yahweh, “For {he is} good, for his covenant faithfulness {is} to eternity,” that the house, the house of Yahweh, filled {with} a cloud,
and the priests were not able to stand to minister from the face of the cloud, for the glory of Yahweh filled the house of God.
Then Solomon said, “Yahweh said he would dwell in a dark cloud.
But I, I have built a house of habitation for you and a place for your dwelling {for} eternities.”
And the king turned his face around, and he blessed all of the assembly of Israel, and all of the assembly of Israel was standing.
And he said, “Blessed {be} Yahweh, the God of Israel, who spoke by his mouth to David my father and fulfilled by his hand, saying,

‘From the day when I brought out my people from the land of Egypt, I did not choose a city from all of the tribes of Israel to build a house for my name to be there. And I did not choose a man to be a leader over my people Israel.
But I chose Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I chose David to be over my people Israel.’
And it was with the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of Yahweh, the God of Israel.
But Yahweh said to David my father, ‘Because it was with your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was with your heart.
However, you, you will not build the house, but your son coming out from your loins, he, he will build the house for my name.’

And Yahweh has raised up his word that he spoke. And I have arisen in place of David my father, and I sit on the throne of Israel, just as Yahweh spoke. And I have built the house for the name of Yahweh, the God of Israel.
And I have put there the Box where the Covenant of Yahweh {is} there, which he cut with the sons of Israel.”
And he stood to the face of the altar of Yahweh, in front of all of the assembly of Israel, and he spread out his palms

(for Solomon had made a platform of bronze, and he had placed it in the midst of the court, five cubits {was} its length and five cubits {was} its width and three cubits {was} its height), and he stood on it, and he knelt on his knees in front of all of the assembly of Israel, and he spread out his palms toward the heavens

and he said, “Yahweh, the God of Israel, no god {is} like you in the heavens or on the earth, keeping the covenant and covenant faithfulness with your servants walking to your face with all of their heart,
which you have kept for your servant David, my father, what you spoke to him. And you spoke with your mouth, and by your hand you fulfilled, as this day.

And now, Yahweh, the God of Israel, keep for your servant David, my father, what you spoke to him, saying, ‘A man to you will not be cut off from to my face, sitting on the throne of Israel, if only your sons will keep their way, to walk in my law, just as you have walked to my face.’
And now, Yahweh, God of Israel, may your word be confirmed that you spoke to your servant David.
But will God truly dwell with man on the earth? Behold, the heavens and the heavens of the heavens do not contain you. How much less this house that I have built!
Yet turn to the prayer of your servant and to his supplication, Yahweh my God, to listen to the cry and to the prayer that your servant is praying to your face,
that your eyes may be opened to this house day and night, to the place {about} which you said you would put your name there, to listen to the prayer that your servant will pray toward this place.

And may you listen to the supplication of your servant and your people Israel that they will pray toward this place. And you, may you hear from the place of your dwelling, from the heavens, and may you hear and forgive.
If a man sins against his neighbor, and he lifts an oath against him to adjure him, and an oath comes to the face of your altar in this house,
then you, may you hear from the heavens and act and judge your servants, to condemn the wicked, to put his way on his head, and to acquit the righteous, to give to him according to his righteousness.

And if your people Israel are struck to the face of an enemy because they have sinned against you, and they turn back and they confess your name and they pray and they supplicate to your face in this house,
then you, may you hear from the heavens, and may you forgive the sin of your people Israel and bring them back to the land that you gave to them and to their fathers.

When the heavens are restrained and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, and they pray toward this place and they confess your name, they turn back from their sin because you have afflicted them,

then you, may you hear {from} the heavens, and may you forgive the sin of your servants and your people Israel, for you teach toward the good way in which they should walk. And may you give rain on your land that you have given to your people for an inheritance.
If famine is in the land, if {there} is pestilence, if {there} is blight, mildew, locust, grasshopper, if his enemy makes it narrow to him in the land of his gates, any plague, any sickness,
any prayer, any supplication that is to any man, to any of your people Israel who know, a man, his plague and his suffering, and he spreads out his palms toward this house,

then you, may you hear from the heavens, the place of your dwelling, and may you forgive, and may you give to a man according to all of his ways, for you know his heart. For you, you alone, you know the heart of the sons of man,
so that they may fear you, to walk in your ways all of the days that they {are} alive on the face of the land that you gave to our fathers.

And also, concerning the foreigner, he who {is} not from your people Israel, and he comes from a distant land because of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm, and he comes and prays toward this house,

then you, may you hear from the heavens, from the place of your dwelling, and may you act according to all that the foreigner has cried out to you, so that all of the peoples of the earth will know your name, to fear you as your people Israel {do} and to know that your name has been called over this house that I have built.

If your people goes out to battle against its enemy by the way that you send them, and they pray to you {in} the way of this city upon which you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,
then may you hear from the heavens their prayer and their supplication, and may you do their justice.

If they sin against you (for {there is} no man who does not sin) and you are angry with them and you give them to the face of an enemy and they take them captive {as} their captives to a land distant or near,

and they bring back to their heart in the land where they have been taken captive there, and they turn back and supplicate to you in the land of their captivity, saying, ‘We have sinned, we have done iniquity and we have acted wickedly,’

and they return to you with all of their heart and with all of their soul in the land of their captivity, where they took them captive, and they pray {in} the way of their land, which you gave to their fathers, and the city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,
then may you hear from the heavens, from the place of your dwelling, their prayer and their supplication, and may you do their justice, and may you forgive your people who sinned against you.
Now, my God, may your eyes please be opened and your ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
And now arise, Yahweh God, to your resting place, you and the Box of your strength. Your priests, Yahweh God, may they be clothed {in} salvation, and may your faithful ones rejoice in goodness.
Yahweh God, do not turn away the face of your anointed. Remember the covenant faithfulnesses of David your servant.”
And when Solomon finished praying, then fire came down from the heavens, and it devoured the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of Yahweh filled the house.
And the priests were not able to go into the house of Yahweh, because the glory of Yahweh filled the house of Yahweh.

And all of the sons of Israel were seeing the fire coming down and the glory of Yahweh on the house, and they bowed down, nostrils earthward on the pavement, and they prostrated themselves and gave thanks to Yahweh, “For {he is} good, for his covenant faithfulness {is} to eternity.”
And the king and all of the people were sacrificing a sacrifice to the face of Yahweh.
And King Solomon sacrificed a sacrifice of 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep. And the king and all of the people dedicated the house of God.

And the priests were standing at their duties, and the Levites with the instruments of song of Yahweh that King David had made to give thanks to Yahweh, “For his covenant faithfulness {is} to eternity,” when David praised by their hand. And the priests were trumpeting in front of them, and all of Israel was standing.

And Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard that {was} to the face of the house of Yahweh, so that there he made the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, for the altar of bronze that Solomon had made was not able to contain the burnt offering and the grain offering and the fats.
And Solomon observed the feast at that time, seven days, and all of Israel with him, a very great assembly, from Lebo Hamath to the wadi of Egypt.
And they did an assembly on the eighth day, for they did the dedication of the altar, seven days, and the feast, seven days.
And on the day of 23 to the seventh month, he sent the people to their tents, rejoicing and good of heart over the good that Yahweh had done for David and for Solomon and for Israel his people.
And Solomon completed the house of Yahweh and the house of the king. And everything coming into the heart of Solomon to do in the house of Yahweh and in his house, he did successfully.
And Yahweh appeared to Solomon by night, and he said to him, “I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place for myself for a house of sacrifice.
If I restrain the heavens and there is no rain, or if I command to the locust to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among my people,

and my people, over whom my name is called, humble themselves and pray and seek my face and turn from their evil ways, then I, I will hear from the heavens, and I will forgive their sin, and I will heal their land.
Now my eyes will be opened and my ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
And now I have chosen and I have consecrated this house for my name to be there until forever. And my eyes and my heart will be there all of the days.
And you, if you walk to my face just as David your father walked, to do according to all that I have commanded you, and you keep my statutes and my judgments,
then I will raise up the throne of your kingdom, just as I cut with David your father, saying, ‘A man to you will not be cut off {from} ruling in Israel.’
But if you, you turn and you forsake my statutes and my commandments that I have set to your faces and you go and serve other gods and prostrate yourselves to them,

then I will uproot them from upon my ground that I have given to them, and this house that I have consecrated for my name, I will send away from before my face, and I will make it a proverb and a taunt among all of the peoples.
And this house that is exalted to everyone passing by it will be appalled, and they will say, ‘Why did Yahweh do according to thus to this land and to this house?’

And they will say, ‘Because they forsook Yahweh, the God of their fathers, who brought them out from the land of Egypt, and they held onto other gods and prostrated themselves to them and served them. Therefore he brought upon them all of this harm.’”
And it happened at the end of 20 years, {during} which Solomon built the house of Yahweh and his house,
that the cities that Huram gave to Solomon, Solomon built them. And he made the sons of Israel dwell there.
And Solomon went {to} Hamath Zobah, and he was stronger than it.
And he built Tadmor in the wilderness and all of the cities of the storehouses that he built in Hamath.
And he built Upper Beth Horon and Lower Beth Horon, cities of fortification {with} walls, doors, and a bar,

and Baalath and all of the cities of the storehouses that were to Solomon and all of the cities of the chariotry and the cities of the horsemen and all of the desire of Solomon, whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all of the land of his dominion.
All of the people being left from the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, they who {were} not from Israel,
from their sons who were left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel did not finish them, Solomon brought them up for the forced labor, to this day.
But from the sons of Israel whom Solomon did not make servants for his work, instead they {were} men of war and commanders of his captains and commanders of his chariotry and his horsemen.
And these {were} the commanders of the deputies who {were} to King Solomon, 250, ruling over the people.

And Solomon brought the daughter of Pharaoh up from the city of David to the house that he built for her, for he said, “The wife to me shall not dwell in the house of David, the king of Israel, because they {are} holy, where the Box of Yahweh has come to them.”
Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to Yahweh on the altar of Yahweh that he had built to the face of the porch,

even by the matter of a day on a day, to offer, according to the commandment of Moses, for Sabbaths and for New Moons and for the annual festivals three times in a year, at the Festival of Unleavened Bread and at the Festival of Weeks and at the Festival of Huts.

And he established, according to the ordinance of David his father, the divisions of the priests for their service and the Levites for their duties to praise and to minister in front of the priests for the matter of a day in its day and the gatekeepers in their divisions for gate and gate, for thus {was} the commandment of David, the man of God.
And they did not turn from the commandment of the king regarding the priests and the Levites about any matter or about the storerooms.
And all of the work of Solomon was established, from the day of the foundation of the house of Yahweh and unto its finishing. The house of Yahweh {was} complete.
Then Solomon went to Ezion Geber and to Eloth on the lip of the sea in the land of Edom.

And Huram sent to him, by the hand of his servants, ships and servants, knowers of the sea. And they came with the servants of Solomon to Ophir. And they took from there 450 kikkars of gold, and they brought {them} to King Solomon.

Now the Queen of Sheba heard the report of Solomon, and she came to test Solomon with difficult questions in Jerusalem with a very great entourage and camels carrying spices and gold in abundance and precious stone. And she came to Solomon and spoke with him all that was in her heart.
And Solomon declared to her all of her matters, and no matter was hidden from Solomon that he did not declare to her.
And the Queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon and the house that he had built

and the food of his table and the seating of his servants and the service of his attendants and their apparel and his cupbearers and their apparel and his burnt offerings that he offered {at} the house of Yahweh. And no more breath was in her.
And she said to the king, “The word {is} true that I heard in my land about your words and about your wisdom.
But I did not believe their words until when I came and my eyes saw. And behold, half of the greatness of your wisdom had not been declared to me. You have added to the report that I heard.
The happiness of your men! The happiness of these servants of yours, the ones standing to your face continually and hearing your wisdom!

May Yahweh your God {be} blessed, who has delighted in you to put you on his throne as king for Yahweh your God. Because your God loves Israel to establish him to eternity, so he has put you over them as king, to do justice and righteousness!”
And she gave to the king 120 kikkars of gold and spices in great abundance and precious stone. And {there} has not been like that spice which the Queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
(And also the servants of Hiram and the servants of Solomon who brought gold from Ophir brought wood of algum and precious stone.

And the king made the wood of algum {into} staircases for the house of Yahweh and for the house of the king and {into} harps and lyres for the singers. And like them were not seen before in the land of Judah.)
And King Solomon gave to the Queen of Sheba all of her desire that she asked, besides what she brought to the king. And she turned and went to her land, she and her servants.
And the weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was 666 kikkars of gold,
apart from {what} the men of the searchers and the merchants were bringing in. And all of the kings of the Arab and the governors of the land were bringing gold and silver to Solomon.
And King Solomon made 200 beaten-gold large shields (he brought up 600 beaten gold onto one large shield)
and 300 beaten-gold shields (he brought up 300 gold onto one shield). And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
And the king made a great ivory throne, and he overlaid it {with} pure gold.

And six steps {were} to the throne, and a footstool was fastened to the throne with gold. And hands {were} from this and from this to the place of the seat, and two lions were standing beside the hands.
And 12 lions were standing there on the six steps, from this and from this. It had not been done thus for any kingdom.

And all of the vessels of the drink of King Solomon {were} gold, and all of the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon {were} beaten gold. Silver was not reckoned as anything in the days of Solomon.
For the ships to the king were going {to} Tarshish with the servants of Huram. One in three years the ships of Tarshish would come carrying gold and silver, ivory and apes and peacocks.
And King Solomon became greater than all of the kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom.

but you have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and you have made Judah and the dwellers of Jerusalem whore like the whoring of the house of Ahab, and also, you have killed your brothers, the house of your father, the ones better than you,
